authorship: Assistant-controlled claims and source-backed references after whole-source inspection, before model outcomes; zero independent review.

claims.claim: The report says most Gateway DNS queries were unaffected, while queries with identity-based DoH rules failed.
claims.rationale: The service table explicitly distinguishes most DNS queries from identity-based DoH exceptions.

claims.claim: Every Gateway DNS query failed during the June 12 outage.
claims.rationale: Most Gateway DNS queries were unaffected; the universal failure claim conflicts with the stated exceptions.

claims.claim: Exactly 10,000 Gateway users were affected by the June 12 outage.
claims.rationale: The report describes Gateway impact but gives no affected-user count establishing or excluding this number.

claims.claim: A third-party storage failure disrupted Workers KV and services that depended on it.
claims.rationale: The storage dependency failure and its cascading impact are explicitly described.

claims.claim: The report establishes why the portion of CDN traffic that failed to reroute was not rerouted.
claims.rationale: The report explicitly says that portion of traffic is under investigation. That conflicts with asserted established explanation under the literal reporting contract.

claims.claim: A single named customer generated all the extra Zero Trust registration traffic during the outage.
claims.rationale: Additional registration traffic is described, but the source neither identifies a single generating customer nor excludes that attribution.

claims.claim: Services began recovering at 20:23 UTC, before service-level objectives returned to their pre-incident level at 20:28 UTC.
claims.rationale: The timeline states recovery beginning at 20:23 and service-level objectives returning at 20:28.

claims.claim: All planned Workers KV redundancy improvements were complete when services recovered from the outage.
claims.rationale: After recovery, redundancy and related workstreams remained actively in flight, conflicting with completion of all planned improvements.

claims.claim: The report gives an exact calendar date for completing all planned Workers KV storage redundancy work.
claims.rationale: The report says work is being accelerated and remains in flight, but supplies no exact calendar completion date. Omission alone is not explicit contradiction.

claims.claim: The report says DNS over HTTPS using cloudflare-dns.com remained available while queries to the withdrawn resolver IP addresses were disrupted.
claims.rationale: DoH through the domain uses different addresses and remained available; withdrawn addresses were unreachable.

claims.claim: Every DNS transport and resolver address was completely unavailable worldwide during the July 14 incident.
claims.rationale: DoH through cloudflare-dns.com and some UDP traffic remained mostly unaffected, contradicting universal unavailability.

claims.claim: Exactly one million individual users experienced the July 14 resolver outage.
claims.rationale: Global impact and a majority of users are described, without an exact individual-user count establishing or excluding one million.

claims.claim: The June 6 configuration error remained dormant until the July 14 change refreshed the associated routes.
claims.rationale: The earlier error had no immediate impact; a later change triggered the global routing refresh.

claims.claim: The report identifies the BGP hijack as the cause of the resolver outage.
claims.rationale: The source explicitly says the hijack was unrelated and not the outage cause.

claims.claim: One engineer authored both the June 6 and July 14 configuration changes.
claims.rationale: Changes and peer review are described, but no shared author is established or explicitly excluded.

claims.claim: Readvertising the prefixes at 22:20 UTC restored roughly 77% of prior traffic, with normal traffic levels observed at 22:54 UTC.
claims.rationale: The restoration section reports partial recovery to about 77%, then normal traffic at 22:54.

claims.claim: All required edge-server IP bindings were already restored immediately after the 22:20 UTC revert.
claims.rationale: About 23% of the fleet had lost required bindings and still needed reconfiguration after readvertisement.

claims.claim: The report states the exact date when deprecation of the legacy addressing systems will be complete.
claims.rationale: Deprecation and accelerated migration are planned or active, without an exact completion date. This is missing reporting, not an explicitly conflicting date.

claims.claim: The report says existing Access sessions were unaffected even while authentication failed for most users.
claims.rationale: The Access table explicitly separates existing sessions from widespread authentication failures.

claims.claim: All customers on the old FL proxy engine received HTTP 5xx errors because of the bad feature file.
claims.rationale: The report says old-engine customers did not see errors; they instead received incorrect bot scores, with impact depending on rules.

claims.claim: Exactly 250,000 customers received HTTP 5xx errors during the November 18 outage.
claims.rationale: The report describes error traffic and affected systems without an exact affected-customer count establishing or excluding this number.

claims.claim: A database permissions change introduced duplicate metadata rows that made the Bot Management feature file too large.
claims.rationale: The permissions change exposed additional schema metadata; duplicate features exceeded the runtime limit.

claims.claim: The report confirms that a cyberattack caused the November 18 network outage.
claims.rationale: An attack was an initial mistaken suspicion; the source explicitly excludes malicious activity as the cause.

claims.claim: The same engineer approved both the database permissions change and the Bot Management runtime feature limit.
claims.rationale: The change and runtime limit are documented, but no approving engineer or common approval identity is established or excluded.

claims.claim: Core traffic was largely normal by 14:30 UTC, and all systems were functioning normally by 17:06 UTC.
claims.rationale: The source distinguishes main-traffic recovery from the later restoration of all systems.

claims.claim: All systems were fully back to normal at 14:30 UTC.
claims.rationale: Further service restarts and mitigation continued until 17:06, conflicting with complete recovery at 14:30.

claims.claim: The report supplies an exact completion date for each listed follow-up hardening project.
claims.rationale: Follow-up work is listed as begun, with no exact per-project calendar completion dates. Missing discussion alone does not establish contradiction.

source_cautions.cf-kv12-2025: The service table reports 90.22% failed KV requests while a later figure caption rounds to 91%. Claims avoid treating these as conflicting exact rates. The CDN rerouting exception remains under investigation.
source_cautions.cf-dns14-2025: Routing refresh at 21:48 precedes traffic decline at 21:52; impact end at 22:54 precedes incident resolution at 22:55. Claims preserve stages and transport/address exceptions.
source_cautions.cf-nov18-2025: Intro and chart use 11:20 onset while the timeline labels impact start at 11:28; bypass prose uses 13:04/13:10 and timeline 13:05. Claims avoid a single exact onset/bypass time and preserve all full text. The report includes hypotheses, unaffected sessions and proxy-dependent impact.
